questions.q: When Britain declared war on Germany in 1914, Canada was also at war.
questions.e: Most Canadians were proud to be part of the British Empire. When Britain declared war in 1914, Canada was at war too.

questions.q: About how many Canadians and Newfoundlanders served in the First World War (1914–1918)?
questions.e: Out of a population of 8 million, more than 600,000 Canadians and Newfoundlanders served in the First World War.

questions.q: Which battle in April 1917 has come to symbolize Canada's coming of age as a nation?
w: The Battle of the Plains of Abraham
questions.e: On April 9, 1917, the Canadian Corps captured Vimy Ridge. About 10,000 Canadians were killed or wounded. Vimy has come to symbolize Canada's coming of age as a nation.

questions.q: About how many Canadians were killed or wounded at the Battle of Vimy Ridge?
questions.e: Canadians captured Vimy Ridge in April 1917 at a cost of about 10,000 killed or wounded.

questions.q: Who was Canada's greatest soldier in the First World War?
questions.e: General Sir Arthur Currie was Canada's greatest soldier in the First World War.

questions.q: What was the series of Canadian victories at the end of the First World War called?
questions.e: The Canadian Corps led a series of victories in the final months of the war, known as 'Canada's Hundred Days'.

questions.q: During the First World War, thousands of former Austro-Hungarian subjects, mainly Ukrainians, were interned as 'enemy aliens' in Canada.
questions.e: From 1914 to 1920, Ottawa interned more than 8,000 former Austro-Hungarian subjects, mainly Ukrainian men, as 'enemy aliens' in 24 labour camps.

questions.q: About how many Canadians were killed in the First World War?
questions.e: More than 60,000 Canadians were killed and 170,000 were wounded in the First World War.

questions.q: On which date is Remembrance Day?
questions.e: On November 11, Remembrance Day, Canadians remember the sacrifice of veterans and brave men and women who served in wars, up to the present day.

questions.q: What do Canadians wear on Remembrance Day?
questions.e: Canadians wear the red poppy and observe a moment of silence on the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month.

questions.q: Which poem, written in 1915 by Lieutenant Colonel John McCrae, is read on Remembrance Day?
questions.e: Lieutenant Colonel John McCrae, a medical officer, wrote the poem 'In Flanders Fields' in 1915. It is often recited on Remembrance Day.

questions.q: At what time do Canadians observe a moment of silence on Remembrance Day?
questions.a: At the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month
w: At 9 a.m. on the first Monday of September
questions.e: The First World War ended with the Armistice at 11 a.m. on November 11, 1918. Canadians observe a moment of silence at that time each year.

questions.q: Which was the first province to give women the right to vote, in 1916?
questions.e: In 1916, Manitoba became the first province to grant voting rights to women.

questions.q: Who was the first Canadian woman to practise medicine in Canada and the founder of the women's suffrage movement?
questions.e: Dr. Emily Stowe was the first Canadian woman to practise medicine in Canada and founded the women's suffrage movement in Canada.

questions.q: Which group of women were among the first to get the right to vote in federal elections in 1917?
questions.a: Nurses serving at the war front
w: Women who owned land in Quebec
questions.e: In 1917, the federal government of Sir Robert Borden gave women the right to vote in federal elections, first to nurses at the war front, then to women related to men in active wartime service.

questions.q: In 1918, most Canadian women of what age got the right to vote in federal elections?
questions.e: In 1918, most Canadian female citizens aged 21 and over were granted the right to vote in federal elections.

questions.q: In which year did Quebec give women the right to vote?
questions.e: In 1940, Quebec granted women the vote.

questions.q: Who was the first woman elected to the House of Commons, in 1921?
questions.e: Agnes Macphail, a farmer and teacher, became the first woman MP in 1921.

questions.q: Canadian women got the right to vote in federal elections before the First World War began.
questions.e: Women first got the federal vote in 1917–1918, during and at the end of the First World War, thanks partly to the work of the suffrage movement.

questions.q: What was the economic crisis of the 1930s called?
questions.e: The stock market crash of 1929 led to the Great Depression, or 'the Dirty Thirties'.

questions.q: How high did unemployment reach in Canada in 1933?
questions.e: During the Great Depression, unemployment reached 27% in 1933 and many businesses were wiped out.

questions.q: What was created in 1934 to manage the money supply and bring stability to the financial system?
questions.e: The Bank of Canada, a central bank to manage the money supply and bring stability to the financial system, was created in 1934.

questions.q: Unemployment insurance was introduced by the federal government in 1940.
questions.e: Unemployment insurance was introduced by the federal government in 1940. Old age pensions and other social programs also grew in this period.

questions.q: About how many Canadians and Newfoundlanders served in the Second World War (1939–1945)?
questions.e: More than one million Canadians and Newfoundlanders served in the Second World War, out of a population of 11.5 million. 44,000 were killed.

questions.q: About how many Canadians were killed in the Second World War?
questions.e: More than one million served in the Second World War and 44,000 were killed.

questions.q: On D-Day, June 6, 1944, which beach did about 15,000 Canadian troops capture?
questions.e: On D-Day, June 6, 1944, 15,000 Canadian troops stormed and captured Juno Beach from the German army in the Allied invasion of Normandy.

questions.q: Which country did Canadians help liberate in 1944–45?
questions.e: Canadians helped liberate Italy in 1943–44 and the Netherlands in 1944–45.

questions.q: Where did Canadian soldiers try and fail to defend against a Japanese attack in 1941?
questions.e: Canadian soldiers took part in the unsuccessful defence of Hong Kong against attack by Imperial Japan in 1941.

questions.q: Where did Canada suffer heavy losses in a failed raid on Nazi-controlled France in 1942?
questions.e: In 1942 Canada suffered heavy losses in a failed raid on Nazi-controlled Dieppe on the coast of France.

questions.q: By the end of the Second World War, Canada had one of the largest navies in the world.
questions.e: The Royal Canadian Navy saw its finest hour in the Battle of the Atlantic, protecting convoys of merchant ships. By the end of the war Canada had the third-largest navy in the world.

questions.q: In which battle did the Royal Canadian Navy protect convoys of ships carrying supplies to Britain?
questions.e: The Royal Canadian Navy saw its finest hour in the Battle of the Atlantic, protecting convoys from German submarines.

questions.q: During the Second World War, many Japanese Canadians were forced from their homes and the government later apologized.
questions.e: Japanese Canadians were relocated and their property was sold without compensation. The government apologized in 1988.

questions.q: Where was oil discovered in 1947, helping Canada's economy grow?
questions.e: The discovery of oil in Alberta in 1947 began Canada's modern energy industry.

questions.q: Which defence alliance did Canada help found in 1949?
questions.e: Canada joined with other democratic countries of the West to form the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) in 1949.

questions.q: In which war in Asia did Canada take part from 1950 to 1953?
questions.e: Canada took part in the UN-led Korean War (1950–53). About 26,000 Canadians served and 500 died.

questions.q: Canada has taken part in many United Nations peacekeeping missions.
questions.e: Canada has participated in many UN operations, including peacekeeping, and in international security missions such as in Afghanistan.

questions.q: In which year were Aboriginal people given the right to vote in federal elections?
questions.e: Aboriginal people were granted the vote in 1960.

questions.q: What was the period of rapid change in Quebec in the 1960s called?
questions.e: The 1960s in Quebec were known as the Quiet Revolution, a time of rapid change. Many Quebecers sought to separate from Canada.

questions.q: Which international organization of French-speaking countries did Canada help found in 1970?
questions.e: In 1970 Canada helped found La Francophonie, an international association of French-speaking countries.

questions.q: In a referendum in 1995, Quebecers voted narrowly to stay in Canada.
questions.e: Referendums on Quebec sovereignty were held in 1980 and 1995. Both were defeated, the second by a very narrow margin.

questions.q: What did the federal government set up in 1963 to study English-French relations?
questions.a: The Royal Commission on Bilingualism and Biculturalism
questions.e: In 1963 Parliament established the Royal Commission on Bilingualism and Biculturalism. This led to the Official Languages Act of 1969.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister was in office when the Constitution was brought home (patriated) in 1982 with the Charter of Rights and Freedoms?
questions.e: In 1982 the Constitution was amended without the agreement of Quebec under Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau. The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms became part of it.

questions.q: Quebec did not agree to the constitutional changes of 1982.
questions.e: The Constitution was amended in 1982 without the agreement of Quebec.

questions.q: Which award did the UN give to the people of Canada in 1986 for welcoming refugees?
questions.e: Canada welcomed thousands of refugees, including Vietnamese 'boat people'. In 1986 the UN High Commissioner for Refugees awarded the Nansen Medal to the people of Canada.

questions.q: After the Second World War, many people from Europe came to Canada to build new lives.
questions.e: Hundreds of thousands of people came from Europe after the war, including refugees from Communist countries such as Hungary in 1956.

questions.q: What was the Group of Seven?
questions.a: A group of famous Canadian landscape painters, founded in 1920
w: The first seven provinces of Canada
questions.e: The Group of Seven, founded in 1920, developed a style of painting to capture the rugged wilderness landscape of Canada.

questions.q: Which Canadian artist painted the forests and Aboriginal villages of the West Coast?
questions.e: Emily Carr painted the forests and Aboriginal artifacts of the West Coast.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Anne of Green Gables'?
questions.e: Lucy Maud Montgomery wrote 'Anne of Green Gables', set in Prince Edward Island.

questions.q: Who invented basketball in 1891?
questions.e: Canadian James Naismith invented basketball in 1891.

questions.q: Who began the 'Marathon of Hope' run across Canada in 1980 to raise money for cancer research?
questions.e: In 1980, Terry Fox, who lost his right leg to cancer at age 18, began a cross-country run, the 'Marathon of Hope', to raise money for cancer research. He became a hero to Canadians.

questions.q: Who travelled around the world in a wheelchair to raise money for spinal cord research?
questions.e: Rick Hansen circled the globe in a wheelchair (the 'Man in Motion' World Tour) to raise money for spinal cord research.

questions.q: Who won the Olympic gold medal and set a world record in the 100-metre race in 1996?
questions.e: Donovan Bailey became a world record holder and Olympic gold medallist in the men's 100-metre race in 1996.

questions.q: Who is a world champion wheelchair racer and Paralympic gold medallist?
questions.e: Chantal Petitclerc is a world champion wheelchair racer and Paralympic gold medallist.

questions.q: Who is called one of the greatest hockey players of all time?
questions.e: Wayne Gretzky is known as one of the greatest hockey players of all time.

questions.q: Which Canadians discovered insulin, a medicine used to treat diabetes?
questions.a: Sir Frederick Banting and Charles Best
w: Alexander Graham Bell and Joseph-Armand Bombardier
questions.e: Sir Frederick Banting of Toronto and Charles Best discovered insulin, a hormone to treat diabetes, which has saved millions of lives.

questions.q: Who invented the telephone?
questions.e: Alexander Graham Bell came up with the idea for the telephone at his summer house in Canada.

questions.q: Who invented the snowmobile?
questions.e: Joseph-Armand Bombardier invented the snowmobile, a light winter vehicle.

questions.q: Who invented the first cardiac pacemaker?
questions.e: Dr. John A. Hopps invented the first cardiac pacemaker, used today to save the lives of people with heart problems.

questions.q: Who was a famous brain surgeon at McGill University in Montreal?
questions.e: Dr. Wilder Penfield was a pioneering brain surgeon at McGill University and was known as 'the greatest living Canadian'.

questions.q: What did SPAR Aerospace and the National Research Council develop for the space shuttle?
questions.e: SPAR Aerospace and the National Research Council invented the Canadarm, a robotic arm used in outer space.

questions.q: Which wireless device was invented by Mike Lazaridis and Jim Balsillie of Research In Motion?
questions.e: Mike Lazaridis and Jim Balsillie of Research In Motion (RIM) invented the BlackBerry, a world-famous wireless communication device.

questions.q: Canada stayed out of the First World War.
questions.e: More than 600,000 Canadians and Newfoundlanders served in the First World War.

questions.q: On D-Day, Canadian troops landed at Omaha Beach.
questions.e: On D-Day, June 6, 1944, about 15,000 Canadian troops captured Juno Beach.

questions.q: Alexander Graham Bell invented the snowmobile.
questions.e: Alexander Graham Bell came up with the telephone. Joseph-Armand Bombardier invented the snowmobile.
